Title: AI Safety Fellowship
Description: The AI Safety Initiative (AISI) at Georgia Tech is hosting our AI Safety Fellowship this Spring, and we would love to invite you to apply! While AI systems become more powerful, our ability to understand, control and regulate these models remains limited. We believe that managing risks from advanced artificial intelligence is one of the most important problems of our time, and the fellowship program is our best introduction to the technical and policy approaches that are most impactful for managing this risk. As a participant in the fellowship, you’ll join weekly discussion groups on current challenges and solutions in ensuring AI is developed to the benefit of our future.  By the end of the semester, fellows will have the opportunity to join AISI as a researcher to work on projects ranging from a technical workshop paper to a comparative policy analysis. We will continue to run two tracks this semester. Technical Track:  We explore solutions to robustly aligning AI systems with human intentions and preventing catastrophic risks. Technical Track Syllabus Policy Track: We discuss the impacts of transformative AI and approaches to ensuring that systems are developed, deployed and regulated responsibly.  Policy Track Syllabus If you want to learn more about how we can align machine objectives with human values, present and future challenges in AI governance, and the impact you can make, apply before Feb 6! Technical Track – APPLY HERE! Policy Track – APPLY HERE! » Learn more at aisi.dev » Join our Discord server We look forward to seeing your application! AISI@GT
Location: We will have online and in-person options.

Title: AI Safety Reading Group: CODA
Description: Dinner, boba provided for the first 20 who RSVP weekly (before Friday morning!) To avoid food wastage, please only RSVP if you are going to show up. The AI Safety Initiative at Georgia Tech is a community of technical and policy researchers at Georgia Tech aimed at reducing risks from advanced artificial intelligence. As such, we focus on topics including: Interpretability: “How can we make AI decision-making processes transparent?” Alignment : “How do we robustly align AI systems to human values & intentions?” Robustness: “How do we ensure AI systems remain resilient when facing adversarial attacks, novel inputs, or changing environments?” Our recent work includes Alignment Faking Revisited: Improved Classifiers and Open Source Extensions and Patterns and Mechanisms of Contrastive Activation Engineering . An in-depth overview of our research can be found here . The goal of this reading group is to introduce GT’s technical research talent to the above problems, current approaches/solutions, and birth & execute impactful research. This week, we will be discussing the paper: "Unforgotten Safety: Preserving Safety Alignment of Large Language Models with Continual Learning" . Feel free to also review this google doc to catch up on previous readings and to learn more about how the reading group functions! https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SJGSJhLchY5ngct37aF29sKUDgEfU1Qk-lLu3rHWbFE/edit?usp=sharing .

Title: Dinner and Worship @ Grace House
Description: Join us every Sunday night for Dinner at 6:30 and Worship starting around 7pm.  Everyone is welcome to join us so please feel free to stop by for some or all of the evening!     Grace House is a progressive campus ministry within a Lutheran and Episcopal tradition that is deeply rooted in our faith in the Triune God. You do not need to identify as any denomination or faith to participate. We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: uPS seminar series_Prof. Sung-Jin Kim
Description: Invited talk: Prof. Sung-Jin Kim from Department of Mechanical Engineering, Konkuk University, South Korea Seminar title: Automated Filtration and Detection of Bioparticles via Mobile-Layer Microfluidics Abstract: Developing simple, robust, and automated platforms that integrate multiple microfluidic operations into a single device remains a challenge in modern bioanalytical systems. This seminar introduces a microfluidic chip platform that exploits surface-tension-driven flow and mobile structural layers to automate fluid handling processes including transport, mixing, volume metering, and biomolecule manipulation. The platform combines vertically mobile top layers with rotationally mobile bottom layers, enabling precise spatiotemporal control of biochemical solutions and magnetic beads without reliance on complex external instrumentation. This mechanically programmable architecture provides a compact and reliable approach to implementing multistep bioassay workflows. To demonstrate the versatility and clinical relevance of the platform, four representative applications will be presented: Automated filtration and detection of Influenza A virus from clinical swab samples Direct isolation of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from whole blood Size-selective extraction of extracellular vesicles across multiple size intervals Execution of high-sensitivity, multistep immunoassays Together, these examples illustrate how mobile-layer microfluidic automation can provide a scalable alternative to conventional laboratory automation systems, enabling streamlined and accessible bioanalytical workflows for diagnostics and research applications. Please RSVP if attend in person:  https:// forms.gle /PXB6aSAREjPAMgFv9

Title: Palm Sunday @ Grace House
Description: Join us every Sunday night for Dinner at 6:30 and Worship starting around 7pm.  Everyone is welcome to join us so please feel free to stop by for some or all of the evening!     Grace House is a progressive campus ministry within a Lutheran and Episcopal tradition that is deeply rooted in our faith in the Triune God. You do not need to identify as any denomination or faith to participate. We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: ConCave’s Lightning Talks Series featuring Prof. Janina Gosseye
Description: Join us for a special edition of ConCave’s Lightning Talks. This series is a chance to share new research and ideas in Architecture, Building Construction, City and Regional Planning, and Music. If you’re interested in design or innovation, you’re welcome to attend. Our keynote speaker is Prof. Janina Gosseye, Professor of Building Ideologies at TU Delft’s Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment. She has worked in Belgium, Australia, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Prof. Gosseye is the series editor for ‘Bloomsbury Studies in Modern Architecture’ series and holds honorary positions at the University of Queensland and the Australian Institute of Architects. Prof. Gosseye’s research explores the intersection of 20th-century architecture and urban history connect with social and political issues. She has published in international journals and written books on urban design, activism, and architectural history. During the45-minute presentation, Prof. Gosseye will share her research journey, reflect on the institutional support that shaped her path, and discuss career choices in academia. She will also provide valuable insights into research structures and opportunities available at TU Delft for prospective graduate students. After the talk, there will be a Q&A session with Prof. Gosseye. Why Attend? Engage with interdisciplinary perspectives in design Connect with fellow scholars and students Learn about the latest research and career paths in design fields This event is open to all—students, scholars, and anyone curious about contemporary design research.

Title: Maundy Thursday @Grace House

We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: Guru Vandana

Therefore, a Guru is not just an instructor, but a "remover of darkness" who guides a student toward wisdom and self-realization. At Georgia Tech, our professors are the architects of our future. They challenge us to think critically, innovate fearlessly, and persevere through rigor. Our Guru Vandana event is designed to bring the ancient spirit of gratitude into our modern campus life. Title: Dinner and Worship @ Grace House
Description: Join us every Sunday night for Dinner at 6:30 and Worship starting around 7pm.  Everyone is welcome to join us so please feel free to stop by for some or all of the evening!     Grace House is a progressive campus ministry within a Lutheran and Episcopal tradition that is deeply rooted in our faith in the Triune God. You do not need to identify as any denomination or faith to participate. We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: Dinner and Worship @ Grace House
Description: Join us every Sunday night for Dinner at 6:30 and Worship starting around 7pm.  Everyone is welcome to join us so please feel free to stop by for some or all of the evening!     Grace House is a progressive campus ministry within a Lutheran and Episcopal tradition that is deeply rooted in our faith in the Triune God. You do not need to identify as any denomination or faith to participate. We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: Dinner and Worship @ Grace House
Description: Join us every Sunday night for Dinner at 6:30 and Worship starting around 7pm.  Everyone is welcome to join us so please feel free to stop by for some or all of the evening!     Grace House is a progressive campus ministry within a Lutheran and Episcopal tradition that is deeply rooted in our faith in the Triune God. You do not need to identify as any denomination or faith to participate. We seek to subvert the narrative that Christians are bigoted by living out the social justice message of Christ in the Gospels in our daily lives. We are an LGBTQIA+ affirming ministry that believes that God loves people exactly as we are.  We recognize the ways that racism harms people and work to dismantle white supremacy. We understand that science, medicine, and environmental justice are crucial to caring for all of God's creation. We strive to practice trauma informed spirituality. This means that we practice enthusiastic consent and we are a sex-positive ministry that prioritizes mental health and stands with survivors of abuse in all forms. In all of this, we also make sure to leave room for safe inquiry and encourage discussion. Even though we are believing Christians, we do not and cannot claim to have all the right answers. We celebrate other religious practices and value interfaith work. Ultimately, Grace House looks for the best in everyone and strives for justice and equity where we can. This is a safe space for all to feel like they belong.

Title: Summer Town Hall
Description: We are the Aerospace Engineering Graduate Student Association (AE GSA), and we host monthly town halls with free food open to everyone! These events typically start with ~5-15 minutes of updates and are then followed with guided discussions and socializing. We aim to create an environment for all students across all labs, and we serve as a resource students can use to discuss topics relevant to the AE school and student experiences. We work closely with AE faculty to incorporate student feedback into the AE school. Previous discussion topics have included GTA/GRA stipends, PhD Qualifier Exams, navigating a career path as an international student, and more. Stay tuned for our future events!
